core_obligations: Reduce the principal ideal statement: the content ideal, once it exists, is finitely generated, and a finitely generated ideal of a valuation ring is principal (proof lines 5810-5814).

Reduce to the henselization: let A^h be the henselization and let B' be the localisation of the base change at the maximal ideal generated by the two maximal ideals; then the map to B' is flat hence faithfully flat, and since a faithfully flat map is universally injective the membership of an element in an ideal times the module is equivalent to the same membership after the base change (proof lines 5816-5828).

Conclude: the henselization of a valuation ring induces a bijection between ideals that preserves inclusions, so an element has a content ideal over the original ring exactly when its image has one over the henselization; the henselized case is covered by the colimit freeness lemma together with the minimal containment statement, which finishes the proof (proof lines 5829-5836).
proof_roadmap: Existence plus finite generation gives principal content ideals (proof lines 5810-5814).
Faithful flatness after henselization detects membership in ideal multiples (proof lines 5816-5828).
Transfer content ideals along the bijection of ideals of the henselization and use the henselized case (proof lines 5829-5836).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for an essentially finite type local map out of a valuation ring and a finite flat module, every element has a content ideal, which is moreover principal (statement lines 5800-5808, tag 0ASX). The proof is a genuine reduction: the principal statement follows from finite generation and the characterization of valuation rings, while existence is reduced to the henselization by observing that the localisation of the base change is faithfully flat and hence membership in ideal multiples is detected after the change, and then transferred back using the inclusion preserving bijection between ideals under the henselization and the content statement in the henselized case. The faithful flatness reduction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
